neighbours.label: ' even' / ' equally' as a degree word in a comparison, before an adjective or comparative ('even harder', 'equally impressive')
fire: The sequel turned out to be even funnier than the original.
Winters in the north are even colder than people expect.
The second speaker was equally persuasive on the subject.
Finding a flat in the capital is even more difficult these days.
Her later novels are equally admired by critics.
The view from the summit was even better than the photographs.
Losing the key was bad, but losing the map was even worse.
The two proposals seemed equally risky to the board.
quiet: Even the neighbours came out to watch the parade.
Six and eight are both even numbers.
The second speaker was very persuasive on the subject.
He never even opened the letter from the bank.
The cake was divided equally among the six guests.
The view from the summit was far better than the photographs.
She did not even know his name.
The score was even at half time.

notes: Card: ' even' x13, ' equally' x7 of the top 32, always before a comparative or graded adjective. Probes: even harder 0.46, equally talented 0.51; focus 'Even the children' 0.03, 'even number' 0.02, 'much harder' 0.05. The + pole is quantity ' more' ('more than 45', 'more calcium').
